title: _validate_csv_declared_schema_for_profile returns a header list/None that its only caller discards
description: _validate_csv_declared_schema_for_profile is annotated `-> list[str] | None` and threads a `return None` (early exit) plus `return header` (success) and bare `return` after raising paths. Its sole caller (read_source, line 501) invokes it purely for its validation side effects and discards the return value entirely; a repo-wide search confirms no other caller. The CSV read path independently re-derives the schema via _select_columns(lf, ...). The header return value is therefore dead: the function exists only to raise on mismatch. The signature can be simplified to `-> None`, dropping the `header_set`/`return header` plumbing that exists only to satisfy the unused return contract, with no behavior change.
evidence: Grep for `_validate_csv_declared_schema_for_profile` yields exactly two hits: the def (line 227) and the call at line 501, where the result is not assigned: `        _validate_csv_declared_schema_for_profile(\n            path=path_string, ...)`. The function returns `header` (line 283) / `None` (line 236) but nothing consumes it.
est_reduction: ~3-5 lines and a simpler `-> None` signature
behavior_preservation: Pure side-effect (validation/raise) is unchanged; only the unused return value is removed.
